summary: A strong paper: realistic settings, full-length scripts in Parts 2-4, and real IELTS-style traps throughout (a branch code next to the order number, a dining table corrected to a coffee table, three rejected delivery days). One Part 4 gap could fairly be answered two ways, so the key now accepts both.
strengths: Part 1 tests the classic skills: spelling (Nazarova, Cherry), a number read digit by digit with a distractor number (331), and corrections (dining -> coffee table, 100 -> 80 thousand).
Part 2 MCQs reject the obvious options explicitly (centenary, government money; March, July; closing, weekends only).
The Part 2 matching box has two strong distractors that are mentioned and rejected (moved to a new position; longer opening hours).
Part 3 has proper disagreement and self-correction in nearly every question (calculations vs glue drying; drawings rejected as a success).
Part 4 is a coherent academic lecture with notes in the same order as the talk.

issues.problem: The notes line 'each orca family group uses its own ___' can be completed with 'calls' as well as 'dialect': the lecture says 'uses its own set of calls - its own dialect, in effect'. A student writing 'calls' would have been marked wrong.
issues.change: Answer key changed to accept both 'dialect' and 'calls'; explanation updated in the overlay.

issues.problem: Q40 'hydrophones' is followed in the script by the gloss 'underwater microphones'; some students may write 'microphones'.
issues.change: The key is right (networks of hydrophones). Consider adding 'TWO WORDS' wording elsewhere or leave as is; no change made.

issues.problem: Part 1 script is 572 words, slightly short of a typical real Part 1.
issues.change: Optional: one more exchange next time the audio is recorded.
